items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIII, List of Answers on Terminology 102:1
items.html: The hairs that come out from the Mochin of conception are called spikes. And those that come out from the Mochin of nursing are called strands. And those that come out from the Mochin of Gadlut are called hairs. And the hairs of conception extend to the chest, where the Nukva of ZA, Rachel, stands; and those of nursing extend to the throat, where Leah stands; and those of Gadlut stand in their place and do not extend downward, because they do not bestow to another. And the spikes, which extend to the Partzuf of NHY, are the aspect of Hochma — that is, they reveal there the illumination of Hochma from the chest and below, where the Partzuf of NHY begins. And the strands, which extend to the throat, where the Partzuf of HGT stands, are discerned as the aspect of Bina, for the illumination of Hochma is not revealed in the HGT, as is known. And the hairs that stand in their place and do not extend downward are discerned as the aspect of Daat — namely, the aspect of the upper Daat, from which there is no bestowal downward, as above regarding the upper Daat of Arich Anpin (Page 444, Item 13, s.v. 'and this'). Thus the spikes are the aspect of Hochma, the strands are the aspect of Bina, and the hairs are the aspect of the upper Daat — that is, there is no coupling in it to bestow the illumination of Hochma downward.
